lines.en: I love my niece.
She’s the only thing I’ll ever need.
When I’m with her, I feel happy. And when I’m not with her, I can’t stop thinking about her.
It doesn’t matter if she wants me all to herself. Or that she fights away anyone else who wants to see me.
She’s doing it all for good reason — because she needs me in order to function.
It’s the same way I feel about her.
If that’s not true love, I don’t know what is.
She’s such a good girl.
If she cut her finger slicing carrots, I would put it in my mouth and suck on it until the blood clotted.
If I watched her empty rat poison into my supper, I would still eat it because I know she’d never do anything to hurt me and that it’s probably just for flavor.
You have no idea how much I love my niece.
You have no idea how much she loves me.
No one can and no one ever will.
The Ami scene will begin now.
: What do you think you’re doing?! I told you I don’t need any help!
: Who says I’m helping and not just standing around? This is my house and I’m allowed to stand wherever I want.
: It’s my house too, mister. And if I say you’re getting in the way, it means you’re getting in the way!
: Are you trying to tell me you don’t care about my company anymore?
: No. I’m trying to tell you that tonight’s dinner is a surprise and that you’re going to ruin it if you keep watching me.
: It’s not much of a surprise if you’re going to be waving the cookbook around in front of my face like that.
: Hey! Stop looking and go sit down! I’m doing this for you, you big meanie!
: You’re absolutely sure you don’t want any help? I know I’m normally useless, but I can at least mix stuff if I try hard enough.
: And surprises aren’t really my thing in general, so if that’s what’s keeping you from-
: I’m fine. I’m sure you had a long day and that you want to relax now. There’s no need for you to interfere with my job when I never interfere with yours.
: To be fair, I’m not so sure your intellect would allow you to effectively interfere with my job. Leave things like that to Makoto.
: You shut your mouth or I really will pour rat poison into your dinner.
I love my niece.
She reminds me a lot of someone else I used to know.
It’s someone I try not to think about because it hurts when I do.
But it hurts even more to not think about her.
Damned either way, I blank everything out and take a seat at the living room table.
I eagerly await the dinner my wonderful niece is making me.
I’m sure it will be delicious because she understands the things I like and the textures and the colors and the food and the food and niece and did I mention I love her?
I love her so much.
My niece, I mean.
Not the other person I mentioned a moment ago because she isn’t real and you can’t love what isn’t real and oh look Ami is back.
: Curry?
: And lots of it. Good thing we bought that second rice pot, right?
: Ami, this is too much food.
: Then we’ll have leftovers. Who cares? Curry is always better on the second day anyway.
: Fair enough. Is this really so special that I had to step away from the kitchen, though? Anyone can make curry.
: This isn’t just any curry, Sensei. It’s Ami’s special curry — made with real Ami.
: Real Ami?
: It’s full of my blood. I used it in place of salt. I hope you like it.
: As long as it’s not rat poison.
I spoon a spoonful of curry into my spoon and then spoon it into my mouth. I can’t even taste the blood.
Ami’s special curry is way better than anything you can buy from the store and I’m glad she made it for me tonight.
: I love your blood.
: Thanks! I love it too.
: I was just kidding, though. This is normal curry without any Ami in it. But I’m glad to know you would have eaten it if there was!
: If there is no Ami in the curry how can it be called Ami’s special curry?
: It’s special because it’s rare!
: I’ve only made it a few times since I started high school. Which means you should savor it since you have no idea when the next time you’ll get any is.
: Probably the next time I ask. I can’t imagine a world where you’d ever say no to something I want.
: Nuh-uh. There are plenty of things I’d say no to. You just don’t normally ask for any of them because you love me so much. Right, Sensei?
: Yes.
I love my niece so much that I am not opposed to consuming her bodily fluids when she uses them to cook.
I am also not opposed to consuming her and if she shrunk herself down to the size of a pill I would take her with a glass of water, swallow her, and allow her to expand in size inside of me.
You have no idea how much I love my niece.
: Thank you, thank you.
: It’s always so much fun whenever you think out loud. You don’t share your feelings enough and hearing them straight from the source is like heroin for me!
: But of course, I say that as a good girl who has never done and never will do drugs. Because the only drug I need is you.
Awwwwww.
: Teehee!
: You’re lucky I don’t take real advantage of you when you’re like this, Sensei. It would be so easy.
: Like what? What am I doing wrong?
: You’re not doing anything wrong. You’re just probably not doing what you think you’re doing.
: There’s a disconnect between your mind and what’s actually happening that makes things seem normal to you when they’re not like, actually normal.
: It’s a coping thingy.
: For example, you’re totally naked right now and you probably didn’t even realize.
I look down and confirm that I am, in fact, naked.
Whoopsie.
: That’s so weird. Most of my thoughts are entirely coherent right now.
: There have been plenty of times where I’ve blacked out, but this is kind of like a halfway point where I’m still sentient.
: How curious.
: It’s probably because of what I mentioned earlier.
: What did you mention earlier?
: My parents.
: I said something in passing about how you’ve slipped into the dad role perfectly and I guess your brain just kinda kicked itself into self-defense mode.
: It’s my fault for letting it slip. I understand by now that this can happen since the same thing happens to me sometimes.
: It’s true, though. And there’s no harm in saying that now since you’re already like this.
: I don’t want to say you’re more of a dad to me than my real dad ever was, but I definitely like you more.
: Granted, I was always more of a mama’s girl in the first place.
: I didn’t dislike my dad or anything. He was totally...normal.
: But next to Mom, he just...
: No one could ever look good next to her. It wasn’t his fault.
: She was beautiful. Creative. Funny. Smart.
: And the way she treated me...
: It was like nothing else mattered to her.
: Sorry. I know I’m getting emotional when we haven’t even started eating yet, but...
: Honestly, my mind’s been kind of all over the place lately.
: What with those standardized test thingies and...with Maya and Ayane starting to...treat me like I’m some kind of...
: Never mind. We don’t have to get into that right now. I’m more interested in hearing what you have to say about my parents.
: You miss them too, right?
: Of course you do...How could you not when you were hit just as hard by their passing as me?
: But it’s fine. Well...no. It’s not fine. Nothing like that can ever be fine.
: But they’re in a better place now. Or at least I hope they are.
: I know Mom never believed in God.
: She pretended to around me because it was the “right” thing to do, but even when I was little, I could tell she was just going along with it for my sake.
: You feel the same as her, don’t you?
: That there is no afterlife. Or reincarnation. Or...anything at all.
: I don’t like that.
: I can’t stand the idea of the two of them just...covered in dirt for the rest of forever.
: I want them to go somewhere else. And I want to go somewhere else when I die too.
: I know you loved her, Sensei.
: And I’m not just saying that because everybody loved her. I know she was important to you in a way my dad never was.
: And even if you and him never saw eye to eye on stuff, I know you must at least kind of miss him too.
: But he’d be proud of you if he could see you now. And so would my mom.
: You’re doing an amazing job. We both are.
: Which is why I’m going to try harder to be like her.
: To be someone everyone loves and admires. But, more importantly than that...
: To be someone you love and admire. Because what you think matters more to me than every other thought in every other world squished into one giant ball.
: You don’t want that.
: Huh?
: You don’t...
: Want...to...
: Don’t...
: Why not? Why would I not aspire to be someone that important to you? And don’t go saying it’s because you already love me a lot since we both know you can always love me more.
I reach into the back of my mind, unsure of whether or not I’ll be able to latch onto anything and, if I do, if Ami will be able to catch a glimpse of it.
She’s seen almost everything so far. The things I thought were private wound up not being private at all.
I do not know the shape I’m in or the state of my mind. But as someone so accustomed to seeing me this way and at least attempting to fix me up, I hope she’ll understand.
Goodbye thoughts of blood...dismembered carrots.
Goodbye colors, textures, wan’dring rabbits.

In this desperate plea for a voice to speak I clap my hands and stomp my feet but it’s not a tantrum I repeat I’m doing this because I’m weak my throat is hoarse from lack of sleep and this run on sentence hurts to read but-
I can not punctuate something that is meant to look broken.
And I can not place a period in a sentence that is never meant to end.
All I can do is split myself open and hope that some of my guts spill onto Ami.
She’s chasing after something she doesn’t want to find.
And should she ever spot a period...or another ending mark-
I pray she just ignores it.
Thus begins another arc.
: She...
: You...
: Uhh...l...let’s move on!
: We should talk more about how...uhh...
: Uhh...
: Right! Maya and Ayane have been really mean to me lately! Do you want to hear more about that?
: Sure.
: Are you crying?
: What do you mean “Am I crying?!” Things just got really intense and sad all of a sudden and now you’re just going back to normal?! What the heck?!
: What are you talking about? And why am I naked?
: You’re naked because you have a problem! And only I know how to take care of it! Okay?!
: A problem? Are you talking about-
: Maya and Ayane are trying to get rid of me!
: What?
: What do you mean they’re trying to get rid of you?
: I mean they’ve been hanging out without me and...excluding me from stuff and...it’s kind of like they don’t want to be my friends anymore.
: It’s been really, really hurtful.
: I’m just happy I have you still...I know you’d never leave me...
: They’re not trying to get rid of you, Ami. The two of them are just...going through something that you wouldn’t really understand.
: Try me. I’m not as dumb as I look. Or act.
: I’ve been given specific instructions to not do that.
: So it is a secret after all...
: I’m sorry. I just can’t-
: Does it have something to do with “the end of the world?”
: How do you-
: Makoto texted me about it.
: Something about the world being a...loopy thing? She used a bunch of big words I didn’t really get.
: I see...
I guess no one told Makoto to keep Ami out of this.
But, then again, I don’t really understand why we were supposed to in the first place, so...
: Would you mind explaining what all of this is about, Sensei?
: Fine.
: Your first year of high school is never going to end.
: You and everyone else are caught in a timeloop that causes it to start over every few months.
: You retain most of your memories and progress in relationships, but certain information is conveniently omitted from what you carry on from one iteration to the next.
: And seeing as you haven’t interjected yet, I should also inform you that if you try to talk about this to anyone else, that they’ll continuously interrupt you until you change topics.
: Also, everybody disappears, the sky turns red, and pregnancy is probably not the cause.
: Sensei...
: ...Yeah?
: That is the dumbest thing I have ever heard.
: What?
: Did you seriously think I was going to fall for that?
: Ami, it’s not-
: I know I said I’m not as dumb as I look, but to think you thought I was that dumb? Come on! That’s insulting!
: Also, somebody should really give Makoto the memo that this is all just a prank because it really seemed like she was taking this seriously. How can she be so smart and yet so gullible?
: Ami-
: Just eat your dinner, Sensei. It’s getting cold.
: And stop believing everything Maya tells you. She reads too many weird manga and they’re clearly going to her head.
: It’s not just her. It’s-
: And stop believing everything Maya tells you. She reads too many weird manga and they’re clearly going to her head.
: Ami, listen...I have seen-
: And stop believing everything Maya tells you. She reads too many weird manga and they’re clearly going to her head.
: Curry?
: You never make curry.
: It’s Ami’s special curry! Made with real Ami.
: I’m suddenly not hungry anymore.
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
